Grand Willow Hotel Front Desk Supervisor Full-Time Position
The Grand Willow Hotel, a 320-room hotel located in the heart of Lakeview City, is seeking an experienced front desk supervisor to join our team.
Since opening in 1998, we have welcomed guests from more than 80 countries, and we are known for our friendly service and attention to detail.
Our facilities include two restaurants, a rooftop pool, a fitness center, and six meeting rooms that can hold up to 300 people.
Last year, the hotel was named one of the top ten business hotels in the region by Travel Weekly magazine.
The hotel is currently undergoing a renovation of its lobby and guest rooms, which is scheduled to be completed in September.
The successful candidate will be responsible for supervising a team of twelve front desk agents, creating weekly work schedules, and handling guest complaints and special requests.
He or she will also work closely with the housekeeping and restaurant departments to make sure that every guest has a pleasant stay.
We are looking for someone who stays calm under pressure and enjoys solving problems.
Requirements:
At least three years of experience working at a hotel front desk, including one year in a supervisory role.
Excellent communication skills in English; the ability to speak a second language is a plus.
Familiarity with hotel reservation software, such as RoomMaster or StayPro.
Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and holidays when necessary.
Candidates with experience in training staff will be given preference.
We offer a competitive salary, health insurance, paid vacation, and free meals during work shifts.
Employees also receive a 50 percent discount on rooms at any of our sister hotels in North America.
To apply, please send your résumé and a cover letter to Martin Cole, Human Resources Manager, at careers@grandwillow.com by May 20.
Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
Document 2: E-mail
To: Martin Cole From: Emma Rossi Date: May 12 Subject: Application for Front Desk Supervisor
Dear Mr. Cole,
I am writing to apply for the position of front desk supervisor, which was advertised on your hotel's Web site.
I have attached my résumé for your review.
For the past four years, I have worked at the front desk of the Harborside Inn, a 150-room hotel in Portland.
I started as a front desk agent and was promoted to assistant supervisor eighteen months ago.
In my current role, I train new employees, prepare staff schedules, and deal with guest concerns when the supervisor is not available.
Last year, I also led a project to reduce check-in times during busy periods.
By introducing an online check-in option and reorganizing the work schedule, my team was able to cut the average waiting time from twelve minutes to four.
As a result, our guest satisfaction scores rose by fifteen percent.
The project was later introduced at our company's other two hotels in Oregon.
I am also a certified first-aid instructor and have trained all of our staff in basic emergency procedures.
I am familiar with StayPro, which we have used at the Harborside Inn since 2021.
In addition to English, I speak Italian fluently and have a working knowledge of Spanish.
I am particularly interested in the Grand Willow Hotel because of its excellent reputation for customer service.
I stayed at your hotel two years ago while attending a conference, and I was impressed by how quickly and politely the staff solved every problem.
Even when I accidentally locked myself out of my room at three o'clock in the morning in my pajamas, the night manager greeted me as if I were wearing a business suit.
He then calmly opened the door for me and offered me a cup of hot tea.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring the same level of service to your guests.
I believe that my experience in improving guest satisfaction and training new staff members would make me a valuable addition to your front desk team.
I am available for an interview at your convenience and could start working as early as July 1.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely, Emma Rossi
Document 3: E-mail
To: Emma Rossi From: Martin Cole Date: May 23 Subject: Interview Invitation
Dear Ms. Rossi,
Thank you for your interest in the front desk supervisor position at the Grand Willow Hotel.
After reviewing your application, we would like to invite you to an interview.
The interview process consists of two parts.
First, you will meet with me and our general manager, Ms. Helen Park, for about 45 minutes.
After that, you will be asked to take part in a short role-play exercise in which you will respond to a difficult guest.
One of our staff members will play the guest, and we will observe how you handle the situation.
During the interview, we will ask you about your experience supervising staff and handling complaints.
We will also explain the details of the position, including working hours, salary, and benefits, and you will have plenty of time to ask questions.
Please don't worry; our staff member is a much better actor than he is a guest.
We have two time slots available: Tuesday, May 28, at 10:00 A.M., or Thursday, May 30, at 2:00 P.M.
Please reply to this e-mail by May 25 to let us know which time you prefer.
If neither time is convenient, we can arrange a video interview instead.
When you come, please bring a form of photo identification and copies of any relevant certificates.
Interviews are held in the Lakeside Room on the second floor.
Please check in at the front desk when you arrive, and one of our agents will show you the way.
Since you are traveling from Portland, the hotel will reimburse you for your train fare.
Please keep your receipt and submit it on the day of the interview.
If you are offered the position, we will also contact two of your references, so please include their names and phone numbers in your reply.
We look forward to meeting you.
Best regards, Martin Cole
Document 4: E-mail
To: Emma Rossi From: Helen Park Date: June 20 Subject: Welcome to the Grand Willow Hotel!
Dear Emma,
On behalf of everyone at the Grand Willow Hotel, I would like to welcome you to our team.
We were all impressed by your performance during the interview, especially the way you calmly handled the role-play.
Our staff member told me afterward that you were the first candidate to make him laugh.
As we discussed, your first day will be Monday, July 1.
During your first week, you will take part in our orientation program, which is designed to help new employees become familiar with the hotel and its procedures.
Here is your schedule for that week.
Monday: Welcome breakfast with the management team, followed by a tour of the hotel and a meeting with Human Resources to complete your employment forms.
Tuesday: Training on the RoomMaster reservation system.
Although you are familiar with StayPro, our hotel switched to RoomMaster last year, so this session will be important.
Wednesday: A full day shadowing our current supervisor, Kevin Lam, who will be transferring to our sister hotel in Vancouver at the end of July.
Thursday: Meetings with the heads of the housekeeping, restaurant, and maintenance departments.
Friday: Your first shift at the front desk, from 2:00 P.M. to 10:00 P.M., with Kevin available for support.
In your second week, you will begin supervising the morning team on your own, and Kevin will gradually hand over his remaining responsibilities to you before he leaves.
We would also like you to lead a project similar to the one you described in your application, as our guests have recently complained about long lines at check-in on Friday evenings.
We hope to discuss your ideas at the end of your first month.
Please arrive at 8:30 A.M. on Monday and use the staff entrance at the back of the building.
Your uniform will be ready in the staff locker room, so there is no need to bring formal clothes.
Free parking for employees is available in the underground garage; please show your employee ID card to the attendant at the entrance.
Pajamas, of course, are also not required.
If you have any questions before your start date, please feel free to contact me directly.
Warm regards, Helen Park, General Manager
Document 5: Online Review
Grand Willow Hotel Reviewed by Yusuf Demir Rating: five out of five stars Posted: August 14
I stayed at the Grand Willow Hotel for three nights last week while visiting Lakeview City on business.
The room was spacious and spotless, and the view of the lake from the tenth floor was absolutely beautiful.
However, what impressed me the most was the service at the front desk.
On my second night, I realized that I had left my laptop in a taxi with all my presentation materials for the next morning's meeting.
I was in a panic, but the front desk supervisor, Ms. Rossi, immediately took charge of the situation.
She called the taxi company, found out which driver had picked me up, and arranged for the laptop to be returned to the hotel within an hour.
While I was waiting, she even offered to print my presentation from my e-mail in case the laptop did not come back in time.
She also helped a family from Spain at the same time, switching between English and Spanish without any difficulty.
The next morning, she had already arranged a taxi for me, and she handed me a small breakfast box because she knew I would not have time to eat at the restaurant.
My presentation went very well, and my client signed the contract that afternoon.
I also noticed that check-in was very fast, even on a busy Friday evening; I waited less than five minutes although the lobby was full of guests arriving for a wedding.
The lobby itself has been beautifully renovated, with comfortable sofas and a large window facing the lake.
The staff also remembered my name from the first day, which is rare at a hotel of this size.
My only complaint is that the hotel restaurant closes at 9:00 P.M., which is a little early for business travelers who work late.
Fortunately, room service is available 24 hours a day, and the club sandwich is excellent.
I would suggest that the hotel keep the restaurant open at least until 10:00 P.M. on weekdays, or offer a simple late-night menu in the lobby.
I mentioned this to Ms. Rossi when I checked out, and she wrote it down carefully and promised to share it with the restaurant manager.
I will definitely stay here again the next time I am in Lakeview City, although I will try to keep my laptop with me this time.
